/itinerary_variants/0/stops/3/descriptio.source_en: **East Jeju lunch stop** at a guide-vetted local restaurant in the Seongsan / Seongeup / Pyoseon area, chosen to fit cruise day-trip timing. **Two typical options**, selected based on group preference and availability: **(1) Jeju Black Pork Heukdwaeji BBQ** (제주 흑돼지) — Jeju's signature ingredient, the indigenous Black Pig was designated **Natural Monument of Korea** in 2015, and pork-belly cuts are grilled over charcoal at the table with traditional banchan; or **(2) Galchi Jorim** (갈치조림 — braised hairtail with radish, soy-chili sauce) — eastern Jeju's famous seafood dish, drawing on the daily catch from Seongsan and Seongeup-area harbors. Vegetarian options are available at most venues with advance notice (the guide confirms with the restaurant ~30 min ahead). Lunch duration is **~60 minutes**, fitting the cruise day-trip's tight timeline (full day usually 8 hours port-to-port). Beverages: barley tea (free), local **Jeju Beer** (~₩6,000), or **Hallasan Soju** (Jeju's signature distilled spirit, ~₩5,000). All restaurants in the rotation accept **major cards (Visa/Mastercard) + cash KRW**; bilingual photo menus (English/Chinese) are standard at the cruise-tour-vetted venues. Lunch is **NOT included** in the standard cruise tour pricing — typical out-of-pocket is **₩15,000–25,000 per person** (varies by dish); inclusive lunch upgrade available on booking.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/4/highlights.source_en: **Founded 1423** by Sejong the Great — administrative center until **1914 (~500 years)**
**110 traditional structures** within original eupseong walled-town footprint
**Important Folklore Cultural Heritage of South Korea** (entire village + multiple buildings)
**Two ~600-year-old trees** at center: Saw-leaf Zelkova + Japanese Hackberry — **Natural Monuments**
Designed on **Joseon Korean feng shui (geomancy) principles** — typical county-capital plan
**'Dae Jang Geum' (MBC 2003–2004)** filming location — international K-drama hit
**Omegisul (오메기술)** — rice-based Jeju liquor brewed by single family for generations (free tasting)
Historical scars: **1826 fire** destroyed ~80 buildings; **1948 Jeju Uprising** damage
**FREE admission** — village still inhabited by ~250 families maintaining traditions

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/4/whyOnRoute.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ is the main cultural highlight of the east route.** It balances the morning's volcanic scenery with Jeju's human history: stone walls, thatched houses, village trees, old lanes, and local stories. The flat layout works well for a coach group, and the visit gives guests a quieter look at traditional Jeju life before the return drive to the port.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/4/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ (성읍민속마을)** is an inhabited Joseon-era village that preserves old Jeju stone walls, thatched-roof houses, narrow alleys, and traditional household layouts. Historically, the village served as the administrative center of Jeongui-hyeon, one of the main local districts of Joseon-era Jeju, and its heritage value is recognized as an Important Folklore Cultural Heritage site. Unlike a staged folk park, people still live here, so the visit must be respectful and quiet around private homes. The village is also known for its old zelkova and hackberry trees near the center, traditional Jeju household culture, stone grandfather statues, and local stories connected to village life.

~70–80 min from East Jeju via Highway 1132 + Route 16 with one comfort stop
Driver/guide assist with luggage at terminal entrance
Bus #100 connects terminal directly to **Jeju International Airport** (for late flights)

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/5/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The return drive is planned with cruise timing in mind.** From the Seongeup and Seongsan area, the drive back to Jeju Port can take about 70–80 minutes depending on traffic and road conditions, so the route leaves the east coast with a practical buffer before the ship's all-aboard time. The guide monitors timing throughout the afternoon and may adjust restroom or photo time if needed to keep the return comfortable.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/5/descriptio.source_en: Return drive to the **Jeju International Passenger Terminal** (제주항 국제여객터미널) on Jeju City's northern coast. The route from East Jeju (Seongsan/Seongeup area) takes ~70–80 minutes via Highway 1132 (the coastal ring road) and Route 16, with one designated comfort stop. Drop-off is timed to deliver guests to the terminal **at least 60 minutes before your ship's all-aboard time**, traveler-fit the cruise industry's standard buffer for embarkation queues. The vehicle pulls into the **100-bus parking capacity lot**, guests disembark at the terminal entrance with luggage assistance from the driver/guide. If guests have early evening flights from Jeju International Airport, **Bus #100 connects directly from the cruise terminal to the airport** — the guide can advise on this option. The terminal interior offers convenience store, pharmacy, snack shop, souvenir shops with **tax-free items**, Jeju Bank ATM accepting overseas cards, currency exchange (typical hours 08:00–17:00), and SK Telecom T-mobile Wi-Fi rental counter — useful if guests want last-minute purchases or to reload mobile data before sailaway. **Free shuttle bus to Dongmun Traditional Market** (oldest/largest in Jeju City, ~10 min) is also available for any guests with extra time before all-aboard.
